title: Uniqueness of a power-multiplicative algebra norm over a complete ultrametric field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|$. Let $L/K$ be an algebraic field extension: each element of $L$ satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $K$. Let $N:L\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ satisfy $N(x)=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $N(1)=1$, $N(x+y)\le\max(N(x),N(y))$, $N(xy)\le N(x)N(y)$, and $N(ax)=|a|N(x)$ for $a\in K$ and $x,y\in L$. Suppose also that $N(x^m)=N(x)^m$ for every $x\in L$ and integer $m\ge1$. Then $$N(x)=s_{L/K}(x)\qquad(x\in L),$$ where $s_{L/K}$ is the minimal-polynomial spectral norm of [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. No finite-degree, normality or separability hypothesis is imposed on $L/K$.
